## Status
Draft. The eligibility criteria and limits can still change. The protocol will be registered on [OSF Registries](https://osf.io/registries) before screening begins, because PROSPERO does not accept scoping reviews. Registration link: to be added.

## Background

This review maps the factors reported to influence the sharing and reuse of research data in health research, including barriers, facilitators, and governance mechanisms.

Earlier reviews address parts of this topic. Reviews in health and medical research examine incentives [@rowhanifarid2017], principles and norms [@kalkman2019], and governance mechanisms such as harmonized data access agreements [@saulnier2019]. Reviews in public health examine barriers to public health data sharing but exclude research data sharing [@vanpanhuis2014].

This review compares health research data sharing with data sharing in general and in other fields. Beyond health, cross-disciplinary reviews cover what drives and inhibits researchers in sharing and reusing data [@fecher2015; @zuiderwijk2020; @perrier2020].

The taxonomy of factors this review produces serves the CITF-emails study, where it supports manual annotation for supervised machine learning on the emails and identifies factors that the emails cover only in part.

## Objective and questions

The objective is to map the factors reported to influence the sharing and reuse of research data in health research, and to compare them with the factors reported for other fields and for public health data.

1. Which factors (barriers, facilitators, and governance mechanisms) are reported to influence the sharing and reuse of research data in health research?
2. How can these factors be organized into a taxonomy suitable for annotating correspondence about data sharing?
3. How do the factors reported for health research differ from those reported for research in other fields and for public health data?

## Methods

The review follows the scoping review framework of @arksey2005 as refined by @levac2010 and the JBI guidance [@peters2020]. It is reported according to PRISMA-ScR [@tricco2018]. The searches are reported according to PRISMA-S [@rethlefsen2021]. The flow diagram adapts the PRISMA 2020 template [@page2021], with "sources of evidence" in place of "studies".

### Eligibility criteria

The criteria follow the population, concept, and context (PCC) structure that JBI recommends for scoping reviews.

| Element | Criterion |
|:--------|:---------------------------------|
| Population | No restriction. Sources may concern researchers, data stewards, institutions, or governance bodies. |
| Concept | Factors that influence the sharing and reuse of research data, including barriers, facilitators, and governance mechanisms. Research data are data collected for research purposes under ethics oversight. |
| Context, tier 1 | Health research. All source types are eligible. |
| Context, tier 2 | Research in other fields and cross-disciplinary research. Reviews and syntheses only. |

Sources are excluded when they concern only public health data or other health systems data, or only clinical care data. The rule for routine or clinical data reused for research is not yet set. Each source is assigned a tier at screening from its field.

The search covers 2015 to 2025. Language limits are not yet set. Any limit will be stated and justified, as PRISMA-S item 9 requires.

### Information sources and search

One query runs in Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed for 2015 to 2025. It joins two blocks with AND. The first block holds "research data sharing" and related data concepts such as open data, data reuse, curation, and data management plans. The second holds barriers, facilitators, policy, ethics, and infrastructure terms. The query uses no health terms. Each database applies its own journal filter: journal sources excluding trade publications in Scopus, articles and reviews in Web of Science, and journal articles in PubMed. The [search strategy](materials/search-strategy.qmd) page lists the strings.

Citation searching of the included sources supplements the database searches. The final strings are tested against a list of known relevant sources. Every search is recorded on the [search strategy](materials/search-strategy.qmd) page.

### Selection of sources

Records are deduplicated with [ASySD](https://github.com/camaradesuk/ASySD). They are then screened on title and abstract in [ASReview](https://asreview.nl), and again on full text, against the [screening guide](materials/screening-guide.qmd). Exclusion reasons are recorded at full text. Counts at every stage feed the flow diagram.

ASReview ranks records by predicted relevance and starts from a seed sample. The seed is the term "research data sharing" alone, which returned 535 records against 12,188 for the query (4.4%). A seed from a fixed keyword is reproducible.

### Data charting

Each included source is charted once into the form defined in the [codebook](codebook.qmd), with one row for the source and one row for each factor it reports. The form is piloted on a sample of sources and revised before full charting begins.

### Synthesis

The review codes factors inductively. The resulting taxonomy is a primary output. Counts by tier, field, source type, and year describe the evidence base, and the factor categories are compared across fields.

### Reporting and data

The checklists for PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S record where each item is reported. The flow diagram is generated from the screening counts. Search exports, screening decisions, charted data, and all code are in the repository.

## Open decisions

- Language limits.
- The rule for routine or clinical data reused for research.
- The definition of research data, by purpose or by consent.
- The number of screeners, calibration on a sample, and the handling of disagreement.
- Critical appraisal of included sources, which PRISMA-ScR treats as optional.
- Whether any step uses a large language model. Any such step will be reported following the PRISMA 2020 guidance on automation tools and the RAISE guidance.
